mil3.2.8:1.2: “Venerable Nāgasena, when you say ‘name and form’, which of these is name and which is form?”
mil3.2.8:1.3: “Whatever there is that is coarse, Great King, that is form; whatever subtle phenomena of mind and mental factors there are, that is name.”
mil3.2.8:1.4: “Venerable Nāgasena, for what reason is it not name alone that is reborn, or form alone?”
mil3.2.8:1.5: “These phenomena are mutually dependent, Great King, and they arise together.”
mil3.2.8:2.2: “Just as, Great King, if a hen had no yolk, she would have no egg either; the yolk there and the egg there are both mutually dependent, and their arising is together;
mil3.2.8:2.3: in the same way, Great King, if there were no name there, there would be no form either; the name there and the form there are both mutually dependent, and their arising is together.
